title: Moon Base Phases
locator: Lunar Terrain Vehicles, crew/cargo capacity and control modes
role: NASA commissions commercial crew and cargo surface mobility for the lunar south pole.
conditions: Planned open lunar vehicles, Astrolab CLV-1 and Lunar Outpost Pegasus. Crews wear pressure suits.
supports: Model an unpressurized transport with crew seats, cargo space and remote or onboard driving.
limits: Source does not publish an occupied pressure vessel, free air volume, design mass, or combustible inventory for these vehicles.

title: Perseverance Rover Components
locator: Body: Tech Specs; Wheels and Legs: Tech Specs – Wheels; How the Wheels Move
role: NASA and JPL provide flight rover geometry, mass, wheel dimensions, steering and suspension descriptions.
conditions: As-built robotic Mars rover. Exterior dimensions are rounded; the rock-sampling arm extends outside the body.
supports: Set a scale for a six-wheel imaging and sample-collection chassis and illustrate equipment deck, robotic arm and rocker-bogie suspension.
limits: Dimensions bound the whole rover. They do not specify a pressure-vessel volume, crew atmosphere, mass of an individual part, or fire response.

title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires
locator: ICES-2021-266, Table 2, Flight-Sample V-2 column; section III.A and Figure 3
role: NASA Glenn and partners conducted orbital fuel burns in uncrewed Cygnus and measured thin-fabric flame size.
conditions: Saffire V sample 2, cotton jersey, orbital microgravity, forced coflow; the fan was stopped and later restarted. The flame recovered when ventilation resumed.
supports: Use as an observed flame-size reference at the reported material, atmosphere, flow and size. Keep flame size separate from distance burned and spread speed.
limits: Not a partial-gravity rover cabin burn. Changing gravity, material construction, ventilation or mounting breaks direct equivalence. It supplies no whole-cabin heat-release law.

title: Lunar Terrain Vehicle
locator: Lunar Terrain Vehicle Commercial Companies: Astrolab and Lunar Outpost
role: NASA identifies the two LTV providers and their individual lunar vehicle designs.
conditions: NASA public program overview, accessed November 2026. Images include mockups or renderings.
supports: Identify Astrolab CLV-1 and Lunar Outpost Pegasus as separate open crew-transport designs.
limits: Images are not surveyed blueprints or flight measurements. They do not establish cabin air, material properties, electrical loads or exact component positions.

title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test
locator: Sections II and III; Table I, Mylar G at 10.2 psia column; Figure 5
role: NASA reports short-duration partial-gravity flammability tests and separates the surviving and extinguishing oxygen concentrations.

quantities.quantity: Martian-g lowest tested oxygen with sustained flame (ULOI*)
Martian-g highest tested oxygen with extinction (MOC*)
lunar-g lowest tested oxygen with sustained flame (ULOI*)
lunar-g highest tested oxygen with extinction (MOC*)

conditions: Mylar G film; hot-wire ignition; buoyant upward spread under simulated partial gravity in a centrifuge aboard a drop-tower rig. Starred limits use flame survival to the end of a short test.
supports: Compare a single material and pressure under two gravity levels and distinguish tested oxygen brackets from long-duration material qualification.
limits: Earlier lunar results are reproduced in the paper. Different exposure times, surface geometry, forced flow, pressure or fuel can change the bracket. Not a transferable cabin cutoff, spread rate or certification.

title: Canada's Contribution to Mars Science Laboratory
locator: The Maple Leaf on Mars: Canada's Contribution, APXS measurement sequence
role: CSA provided the arm-mounted APXS instrument on Curiosity and funded its operations centre.
conditions: Canadian prelanding engineering description of bringing the sensor head close to a soil or rock target and integrating X-ray counts.
supports: Support an externally mounted contact-science instrument and differentiate a quick survey from a full analysis.
limits: These are approximate integration times, dependent on measurement objectives. They do not specify motor energy, interior fuel, component mass or fire properties.

title: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin (RFM)
locator: Mission overview; ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Rover; Drilling in brief
role: ESA leads the rover mission and describes its mobility, sample acquisition and onboard delivery system.

quantities.quantity: extension rods needed for full reach

conditions: Planned solar-powered Mars surface mission. Each wheel has independent steering and drive.
supports: Represent a robotic mobile drilling lab with flexible wheels, extension rods, sample handling and orbital data relay.
limits: Mission design values do not give measured Mars drilling performance, human-cabin dimensions, or rover fire measurements.

title: First deep drilling success for ExoMars
locator: Opening account; Drill operations; No easy feat
role: ESA reports a sample retrieval by its ground twin at the ALTEC Mars Terrain Simulator in Turin.
conditions: A gravity-offloaded rover test model on Earth sampled medium-hard cemented clay in a layered test well.
supports: Provide a measured drill demonstration with substitute terrain and a sample transferred into the rover laboratory.
limits: The rig offloaded vehicle weight. It did not reproduce the complete Mars environment or prove the same depth on Mars.

title: Chandrayaan-3 Details
locator: Overall specifications: Mass, Power generation, Communication; Rover Payloads
role: ISRO publishes the mass, power generation rating, communications path and instrument list for the Chandrayaan-3 rover.
conditions: Lunar robotic rover, designed for one lunar day. Relays data through the lander. Rover payloads include APXS and LIBS.
supports: Provide a compact lunar rover comparison and distinguish electrical power generation in watts from battery storage in watt-hours.
limits: The 50 W value is a generation rating. This source does not give time-resolved output, battery storage, a crew cabin or material flammability.

title: ExoMars
locator: Italian contribution, MA_MISS; International agreements, drilling system
role: ASI describes Italian instrument and industrial contributions, including INAF-IAPS collaboration on Ma_MISS in the drill.
conditions: ExoMars payload design: observe the borehole wall spectroscopically during drilling.
supports: Support an Italian drill-integrated sensor that interrogates layers in place and distinguishes a sensor in the drill from a camera on the mast.
limits: Historical ASI page contains superseded launch dates. Use this source for payload architecture; drill depth is design reach, and no borehole data from Mars is reported here.

title: Inside development of the crewed pressurized rover for Artemis (JAXA engineering interview, in Japanese)
locator: 31 March 2026; section 過酷な月面でも宇宙飛行士が快適に過ごせるように, answers on thermal control and environmental control
role: JAXA’s habitat thermal and life-support engineer describes the pressurized rover being developed with Toyota.
conditions: Preliminary design reported in March 2026. Cabin environmental systems regulate pressure, temperature and humidity and remove CO₂. Insulation, pumps and radiators help manage heat.
supports: Distinguish the occupied pressure vessel and its actively controlled atmosphere from an open vehicle or a sealed passive test box.
limits: Public interview offers no cabin pressure setpoint, O₂ fraction, ventilation rate, free gas volume, internal material inventory or validated fire response.

title: JAXA and Toyota Reach Agreement on Consideration Toward International Space Exploration
locator: 12 March 2019; Concept proposal for the pressurized rover being studied by JAXA and Toyota
role: JAXA and Toyota jointly describe their early lunar pressurized rover concept.
conditions: Historical concept dimensions as of March 2019. Toyota hosted this joint announcement, which identifies JAXA as a coauthor.
supports: Compare the scale of an early crewed lunar concept to a robotic chassis and distinguish living space from the vehicle bounding box.
limits: The 13 m³ figure describes proposed living space. Effective free gas volume, final flight geometry, atmosphere, heat removal, and actual component masses require independent evidence.
